title: Tanker Acers hit off Qatar with casualties, UKMTO says
excerpt: The Antigua and Barbuda-flagged tanker was struck about 51 nautical miles north of Madinat ash Shamal on 7 October, with casualties reported.
x_post: Tanker Acers hit by multiple projectiles off Qatar on 7 October with casualties, UKMTO says. #MaritimeSecurity #StraitOfHormuz #Tanker #UKMTO
fact_check_fixes: Added to the excerpt that casualties were reported, matching UKMTO's account of the Acers strike.
Added a key point crediting Vanguard, Splash247 and gCaptain for naming the Acers and noting no attacker has been identified.
Specified in the key point on the Hormuz tanker that the 6 October strike was reported in UKMTO's time-late warning issued on 8 October and that no casualties were reported.
Named the Ever Lovely as Singapore-flagged and Evergreen-operated in the key point, as the facts state.
Added to the key point on the CUL Klang that The Maritime Executive reported it, the crew were unharmed and no group claimed responsibility.

Corrected the article's Hormuz paragraph to give the 6 October strike date and the 8 October time-late warning, and dropped the Panama flag and the 11 injured crew, which belong to the 5 October On Peace strike.
Named the Ever Lovely as Singapore-flagged and Evergreen-operated in the article, matching the facts.
Added the 7 October Qatar strike on the Acers, credited to UKMTO, and kept the 8 October Fujairah tanker fire out of the Acers incident.
Added the 7 October attack on the Singapore-flagged CUL Klang in the southern Red Sea, credited to The Maritime Executive, with the crew unharmed and no claim of responsibility.
Moved the Maran Gas Mystras and Arina A into an Earlier in the week line with their own dates, keeping them out of the lede.
Kept the Aviva dated 6 October with the Haber Denizde account of one seafarer killed and the fire put out, alongside the Odesa administration's report of one killed and seven injured.

lesson (facts): A record the tracker has already rejected can be re-created from fresh articles as a brand new incident: when a new entr
lesson (writing): Name every attack still in the day's facts, older ones in an Earlier in the week line with their dates, and never leave
refused: lesson (facts): Never date an attack from a Telegram channel post or a video release: date it from the outlet that reported the strike,
notes: The Aviva is not a new attack: Turkey's Haber Denizde reported the Marshall Islands-flagged tanker Aviva, owned by Garanti Denizcilik and managed by Bilka Denizcilik, hit in the Black Sea on 6 October with one seafarer killed and the fire put out, matching the Odesa administration's 6 October report of a Marshall Islands vessel loaded with rapeseed oil hit with one killed and seven injured. Do not lead today's brief with it, do not date it 8 October, and do not say no damage or casualty details were given.

The Strait of Hormuz paragraph mixes three events and must be rebuilt. The Panama flag and the 11 Indian crew injured belong to the 5 October strike on On Peace, already reported. UKMTO's delayed warning of 8 October was a time-late report of a crude oil tanker struck on 6 October with no casualties. The paused escort followed the 8 October attack on the Singapore-flagged Evergreen containership Ever Lovely near Oman, whose crew were safe. Say those two events and drop the Panama tanker and the injured figure.

The 7 October Qatar strike on the Acers, with casualties, is inside the 48 hour window and in the facts but the article never names it: give it one line, credited to UKMTO. The 8 October fire on a tanker off Fujairah, the Marshall Islands-flagged Dhalkut in Euronews reporting, is a separate attack and not part of the Acers incident.

The Red Sea and Gulf of Aden section is empty. Name the 7 October attack on the Singapore-flagged containership CUL Klang in the southern Red Sea, shots fired with the crew unharmed and no claim of responsibility, reported by The Maritime Executive, with its own date.

Two attacks in the facts are still missing from the text. The Greek-flagged LNG carrier Maran Gas Mystras, confirmed hit by an unidentified projectile in the Strait of Hormuz on 4 October with the crew safe, and the Arina A, claimed hit by a drone off Trabzon on 5 October with its captain killed, belong in an Earlier in the week line with their own dates, not in the lede.
